pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 1 – The Journey Begins
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Smaller than a dot – not yet formed
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Fertilization hasn't officially occurred yet, but your body is preparing to release an egg. The uterine lining is building up to receive a fertilized egg.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: No noticeable symptoms yet. You may be in the last days of your period or approaching ovulation.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Start taking folic acid daily, avoid smoking and alcohol, and maintain a healthy lifestyle.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Begin taking 400 mcg of folic acid daily before or at the very start of pregnancy.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Avoid all medications and supplements without consulting your doctor first.

notification.title: ✨ Your journey starts now!
notification.body: Get ready for the most beautiful experience of your life. Start folic acid today 💊

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 2 – The Moment of Fertilization
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: A single fertilized cell – smaller than a pinhead
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Sperm meets egg to form the zygote. It begins dividing rapidly and travels toward the uterus.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: No obvious symptoms. Some women feel a mild twinge during ovulation.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Stay calm and relaxed. Avoid intense stress as it may affect ovulation.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Continue folic acid. If you take chronic medications, check with your doctor about their safety in pregnancy.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Extreme heat can affect fertilization – avoid very hot baths or saunas.

notification.title: 🌱 A seed of life is sprouting!
notification.body: A new life may have just been created. You're already an amazing mom 💛

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 3 – Nestling in the Uterus
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a grain of sand – 0.1 mm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Now called a blastocyst, it burrows into the uterine wall and begins producing the pregnancy hormone HCG.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: You may notice light spotting from implantation, which is completely normal.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Continue folic acid. Don't worry about light spotting – it's actually a good sign!
pregnancy_weeks.medical: It's too early for a home pregnancy test. Wait until your missed period.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: If bleeding is heavy with severe pain, see your doctor immediately.

notification.title: 🏠 Baby chose its home!
notification.body: Your tiny embryo is settling into your womb. A true miracle! 🌸

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 4 – Your First Positive Test
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a poppy seed – 1 mm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: The embryo forms two primary layers that will become all body organs. The neural tube begins forming.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Missed period, and you may feel mild fatigue or breast tenderness.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: You can take a home pregnancy test now. If it's positive, book an appointment with your doctor!
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Start looking for an OB-GYN and schedule your first prenatal visit, ideally between weeks 8–10.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Don't take any medication without your doctor's approval – even simple pain relievers.

notification.title: 🎉 Two lines means a baby!
notification.body: The most beautiful news of your life – you're pregnant! 🤰💕

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 5 – A Tiny Heart Starts Beating
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a sesame seed – 2 mm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: The heart begins forming and may start beating. Three primary cell layers develop that will form all body systems.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Morning sickness often begins. Fatigue, breast swelling, and frequent urination are common.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Eat small, frequent meals to ease nausea. Dry crackers before getting out of bed can help a lot.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: If vomiting is severe and persistent, ask your doctor about hyperemesis gravidarum.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Severe fatigue is normal, but rapid weight loss or inability to eat warrants a doctor's visit.

notification.title: 💓 The heartbeat has begun!
notification.body: Your baby's heart is beating for the very first time! You'll hear it soon 🩺

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 6 – Facial Features Begin
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Tiny buds appear that will become arms and legs. Eyes, ears, and mouth begin forming. The brain grows rapidly.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Nausea intensifies, ongoing fatigue, heightened sense of smell. You may suddenly dislike previously loved scents.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Early bedtime is essential. Ask for help from family and don't feel guilty for resting a lot.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Your first prenatal visit covers medical history, estimated due date, and initial blood work.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Bright red vaginal bleeding with cramping requires an emergency visit immediately.

notification.title: 👀 Eyes are forming!
notification.body: Your baby's face is drawing its very first features this week 🎨

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 7 – Brain Growing at Lightning Speed
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: The brain grows incredibly fast – 100 new nerve cells per minute! Tiny arm buds resemble fins. Kidneys begin functioning.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: The uterus grows slightly. Frequent urination increases. Constipation may occur due to progesterone.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Drink plenty of water. Dietary fiber helps prevent constipation. Avoid standing for long periods.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: An ultrasound this week may detect the baby's heartbeat for the first time.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Severe constipation with abdominal pain may need medical advice.

notification.title: 🧠 Brain cells at full speed!
notification.body: 100 new nerve cells every minute! Your baby is smart from day one 💡

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 8 – A Real Embryo
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a kidney bean – 1.6 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: The tail disappears completely. All major organs are forming. Fingers begin emerging. Eyes are wide but fused shut.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Your belly is still flat, but the uterus has doubled in size. Nausea is often at its peak.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: A good time for your first comprehensive prenatal visit if you haven't yet. Start a symptom journal.
food_avoid: Processed meats like salami and hot dogs
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Your first visit includes: due date calculation, full blood panel, urinalysis, blood pressure, and weight check.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: If you take medication for heart, diabetes, or blood pressure conditions, tell your doctor right away.

notification.title: 🫘 Size of a bean!
notification.body: Baby has taken on a fully human shape. A little miracle inside you 🌟

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 9 – Fingers Are Separating
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Fingers separate and become distinct. Muscles grow and baby starts moving for the first time – though you won't feel it yet.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Breasts feel heavier and more tender. Mood swings come and go quickly due to hormones.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Wear a supportive maternity bra. Talking openly with your partner about your feelings really helps.
food_avoid: Peanuts if there's a family history of allergies
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The NIPT (Non-Invasive Prenatal Test) can be done now to screen for chromosomal abnormalities.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Severe mood swings with uncontrolled crying may benefit from professional emotional support.

notification.title: 🖐 Tiny fingers are opening!
notification.body: Baby's little fingers are forming. One day they'll hold yours 🥹

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 10 – End of the Early Embryonic Stage
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: All vital organs are complete – we enter the growth and development phase. The head is still proportionally large. Kidneys produce urine.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: You may notice your clothes fitting tighter around the waist. Nausea may start easing soon.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Start thinking about maternity clothes. Elastic-waist pants are perfect for right now.
food_recommended: Vitamin D from eggs and dairy
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The Nuchal Translucency (NT) scan is done between weeks 11–14 to screen for Down syndrome.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Any lower abdominal pain or bleeding requires an urgent medical visit.

notification.title: 🍓 Strawberry-sized baby!
notification.body: All organs are complete! Baby grows stronger every single day 💪

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 11 – Swallowing and Breathing Practice!
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby swallows amniotic fluid and practices breathing motions. Can open and close its fist. Skin is transparent.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Dizziness and headaches may occur due to blood pressure changes. Hair and nails grow stronger from hormones.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Rise slowly from bed to avoid dizziness. Drink water consistently throughout the day.
food_recommended: Citrus fruits rich in vitamin C
pregnancy_weeks.medical: A blood test to check for pregnancy anemia is recommended at this stage.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Severe headache with ringing ears requires an immediate blood pressure check.

notification.title: 🌬 Practicing to breathe!
notification.body: Baby is gearing up for life outside your womb with full energy! 🫁

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 12 – End of the First Trimester
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Major organ development is complete. The digestive system begins working. The placenta fully takes over nourishing the baby.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Miscarriage risk drops significantly. Nausea retreats for most women. A gentle return of energy begins.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: A great time to share your pregnancy news with family and friends! You've made it through the first trimester.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The week 12 ultrasound clearly shows the baby and measures nuchal fold thickness for early screening.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Abdominal cramps with bleeding at this stage need immediate medical evaluation.

notification.title: 🎊 First trimester complete!
notification.body: The hardest part is over! Nausea is fading and baby is thriving 🌈

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 13 – Second Trimester Begins
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby can now suck its thumb. Primary baby teeth begin forming inside the gums. Vocal cords start developing.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Energy returns for most women. The bump starts showing. Mild lower abdominal pain from uterine stretching is normal.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Welcome to the honeymoon phase of pregnancy! Use your restored energy for planning and baby shopping.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The Quad Screen test is done between weeks 15–20 to detect potential fetal abnormalities.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Mild lower belly aches are normal, but sharp pain warrants medical evaluation.

notification.title: 🥝 Welcome, second trimester!
notification.body: Nausea is gone and joy has arrived! Enjoy every single moment 🌺

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 14 – First Movements!
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby can make primitive facial expressions – frowning and smiling! Kidneys are working and producing urine into the amniotic fluid.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: You may notice skin pigmentation changes (a dark line from the navel). Hair becomes shinier.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Start Kegel exercises to strengthen pelvic floor muscles – beneficial for delivery and recovery.
food_avoid: Very salty foods to prevent bloating
pregnancy_weeks.medical: If you're over 35, discuss chorionic villus sampling (CVS) or amniocentesis with your doctor.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Skin changes are normal, but intense itching on hands and feet should prompt a liver function test.

notification.title: 😊 Baby is smiling!
notification.body: That tiny face is forming its very first smile. Incredible! 🥰

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 15 – Baby Can Hear Your Voice!
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Ears are in their proper position and begin picking up external sounds. Bones harden. Skin is covered in fine lanugo hair.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: The bump is now clearly visible. A healthy weight gain of 1–2 kg so far. Back pain may begin.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Sing to your baby! They can hear you now. Talking and reading aloud helps develop hearing and the brain.
food_recommended: Phosphorus from fish for bone building
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The flu vaccine is safe and recommended during pregnancy.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Sharp pain on one side with difficulty urinating may indicate a kidney infection.

notification.title: 👂 Baby hears you now!
notification.body: Talk to them, sing to them. Your voice is the sweetest music they know! 🎵

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 16 – The Bump Is Showing!
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Eyes respond to light even though eyelids are closed. Baby moves arms and legs with strength. The immune system is forming.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Everyone notices your pregnancy now! You may feel the first fluttery baby movements (like butterflies in your belly).
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Start taking weekly bump photos. These moments won't come back and you'll be glad you captured them.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The AFP blood test may be done now to screen for neural tube defects.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: First baby movements are normal anytime between weeks 16 and 25.

notification.title: 🌟 Your bump tells a story!
notification.body: Baby is moving and playing. Did you feel those butterflies? 🦋

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 17 – Fat Starts Building Up
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby begins storing fat beneath the skin for warmth regulation. The umbilical cord becomes thicker and stronger.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Increased sweating from a higher metabolism. Skin may become oilier or drier.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Use a natural moisturizing cream on your belly to help prevent stretch marks.
food_recommended: Beta-carotene from carrots and sweet potatoes
food_avoid: Frequent consumption of pre-packaged frozen meals
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Monitor blood pressure regularly. A sudden rise combined with swelling may indicate preeclampsia.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Sudden severe facial or hand swelling is a medical emergency.

notification.title: 🍐 Pear-sized baby!
notification.body: Baby's tiny fat deposits are forming to keep them warm. So precious! 🤗

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 18 – The Big Anatomy Scan
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a bell pepper – 14.2 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby hears clearly and responds to sounds. Can yawn and stretch. Genitalia are now clearly visible on ultrasound.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Baby movements become clearer. Back pain increases. Round ligament pain (sides of the belly) is common.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Book your anatomy scan (weeks 18–22). This ultrasound checks for structural abnormalities.
food_recommended: Choline from eggs (vital for baby's brain)
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The anatomy scan (Level 2 ultrasound) is the most important scan of the second trimester. Don't miss it.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: If your doctor recommends bed rest, please don't ignore the advice.

notification.title: 🔍 Time for the big scan!
notification.body: You'll see baby fully and maybe find out the gender! 👶

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 19 – Baby's Protective Coating
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Vernix caseosa (a waxy coating) forms to protect baby's skin from amniotic fluid. Baby is very active.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Dizziness and fainting are possible. The growing uterus presses on veins, lowering blood pressure when standing up quickly.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Sleep on your left side to improve blood flow to the baby. Place a pillow between your knees for comfort.
food_recommended: Vitamin C with iron for better absorption
food_avoid: Tea and coffee with iron-rich meals (they block absorption)
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Ask your doctor to go over the anatomy scan results in detail if you've already had it.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Sudden dizziness with chest pain or shortness of breath requires immediate evaluation.

notification.title: 🥭 Mango-sized miracle!
notification.body: Baby's skin is getting its own special protective coating. Nature is amazing! 🌿

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 20 – Halfway There! 🎉
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: The midpoint of pregnancy! Baby swallows amniotic fluid and practices digestion. Fingerprints are forming. Sleep and wake cycles are visible.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: The uterus is now near your navel level. You've likely gained 4–5 kg. Baby movements are felt clearly.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Celebrate this milestone! Half the journey is done. Now start planning the nursery.
food_recommended: Vitamin D from sunlight and food
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Schedule your glucose screening test between weeks 24–28 to check for gestational diabetes.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: No baby movement felt for over 12 hours – call your doctor.

notification.title: 🎉 Halfway there!
notification.body: 20 weeks behind you, 20 ahead. You are absolutely amazing! 💪❤️

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 21 – Senses Are Awakening
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby can taste flavors through amniotic fluid. They prefer sweet and make faces at sour! Senses are developing fast.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Heartburn may begin. The growing uterus pushes on the stomach, forcing acid upward.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Avoid lying down right after eating. Elevate your head slightly while sleeping. Small meals help with heartburn.
food_avoid: Dark chocolate if it triggers heartburn
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Iron deficiency is very common now. Request a CBC blood test to check hemoglobin levels.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Heartburn with difficulty swallowing warrants a medical visit.

notification.title: 👅 Baby tastes what you eat!
notification.body: What you eat reaches baby through amniotic fluid. Feed them well! 🍽️

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 22 – Eyes Opening
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a corn on the cob – 27.8 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Eyelids begin opening and closing. Baby responds to strong light outside the womb. Hair on the head starts growing.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: White vaginal discharge is normal at this stage due to hormonal changes.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Shine a gentle light toward your belly and watch the reaction. It's a fun way to stimulate baby's senses.
food_recommended: Iodine from ocean fish for thyroid development
food_avoid: Excess vitamin A from animal sources
pregnancy_weeks.medical: See your doctor if discharge is colored or has an unusual odor.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Pink or bloody discharge after week 20 needs immediate evaluation.

notification.title: 👁 Eyes are opening!
notification.body: Baby's eyes are searching for light. Send them a warm hello from your heart! ✨

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 23 – A Fighting Chance Outside the Womb
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a small mango – 28.9 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby now has a chance of survival outside the womb with intensive medical support. Lungs are developing rapidly. Hearing is very developed.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Back pain worsens. You may experience Braxton Hicks contractions (practice contractions).
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Learn the difference between Braxton Hicks (irregular, painless) and real labor (regular, intensifying).
food_avoid: High-histamine foods if you have allergies
pregnancy_weeks.medical: If you experience regular contractions before week 37, call your doctor immediately – it may be preterm labor.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: More than 4 contractions per hour is a medical emergency.

notification.title: 💪 Baby is fighting to grow!
notification.body: Every day inside your womb makes baby stronger. You're a hero! 🦸‍♀️

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 24 – Gestational Diabetes Screening
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of an ear of corn – 30 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby is beginning to recognize dad's voice! The brain develops rapidly with folding grooves. Facial features are now complete.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Feet and ankles may swell by the end of the day. This is normal if it improves with rest.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Elevate your feet above heart level when sitting. Avoid prolonged standing. Regular walking improves circulation.
food_recommended: Low glycemic index foods like oats
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Gestational diabetes screening (GCT or OGTT) is done between weeks 24–28. Do not skip this test!
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Blurred vision with severe headache and sudden swelling may indicate preeclampsia.

notification.title: 🍬 Sugar test matters!
notification.body: Don't forget your gestational diabetes screening this week. For you and baby 🩸

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 25 – Learning to Breathe
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Lungs develop surfactant (the substance that keeps air sacs from collapsing). Head hair grows thicker.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Insomnia begins visiting some moms. Finding a comfortable sleeping position with a big belly becomes harder.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: A U- or C-shaped pregnancy pillow helps enormously. Avoid sleeping on your back after week 20.
food_recommended: Natural melatonin from cherries and bananas
food_avoid: Coffee and tea in the afternoon
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Ask your doctor about the Tdap vaccine (whooping cough), which is recommended in the third trimester.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Persistent severe insomnia is worth discussing with your doctor for safe solutions.

notification.title: 😴 How's your sleep?
notification.body: Baby sleeps 20 hours a day! How about you? Take that nap guilt-free 💤

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 26 – Eyes Fully Open
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Eyes fully open and respond to light by moving or squinting. The immune system receives antibodies from mom through the placenta.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Braxton Hicks contractions repeat more often. Mild shortness of breath may occur as the uterus grows.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Deep breathing exercises help you relax and ventilate your lungs. Just 5 minutes daily makes a difference.
food_recommended: Chickpeas and fava beans for plant protein
food_avoid: Cold deli meats that aren't heated
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Blood pressure checks at every visit are critically important heading into the third trimester.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Sudden severe shortness of breath with chest pain is a medical emergency.

notification.title: 👀 Eyes can see you from inside!
notification.body: Baby sees light filtering through your belly. Shine a light! 🔦

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 27 – End of the Second Trimester
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby sleeps and wakes in regular patterns. Brain grows and folds its layers. The immune system strengthens.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Fatigue returns. Back and feet ache more. Mild facial swelling may appear.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Start learning about labor stages and birthing techniques. Enroll in a childbirth preparation class.
food_recommended: Fatty fish like sardines and salmon
pregnancy_weeks.medical: After week 28, start monitoring daily fetal movement (10 movements in 2 hours).
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Not feeling usual fetal movement – call your doctor right away.

notification.title: 🎊 Two trimesters done!
notification.body: You've completed two-thirds of the journey! The finish line is close 🏁

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 28 – Third Trimester Begins
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby blinks, moves its head, and raises its eyebrows! The brain grows remarkably from the outside inward.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Sleep gets harder. Ankles and feet swell more. Colostrum (first breast milk) may start being produced.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: If driving long distances, stop every two hours to walk. Sitting too long increases the risk of blood clots.
food_recommended: At least 2 liters of water daily
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Prenatal visits become every two weeks from now. RH factor antibody check if you're RH negative.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Sudden facial swelling with headache and vision changes = immediate medical emergency.

notification.title: 🌅 Third trimester is here!
notification.body: Last 12 weeks! Baby is growing incredibly fast now 🚀

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 29 – Bones Are Hardening
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a large zucchini – 38.6 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Bones are solidifying and demanding large amounts of calcium. The head grows to accommodate the expanding brain.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Shortness of breath worsens. Heartburn continues. Many moms experience restless leg syndrome at night.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: A warm bath before bed eases leg muscles. Magnesium may help reduce nighttime leg cramps.
food_recommended: Vitamin K2 to direct calcium to bones
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Ask your doctor about baby's position. By now, baby should be starting to rotate for delivery.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Painful nighttime leg cramps with redness and swelling may indicate a blood clot.

notification.title: 🦴 Bones getting stronger!
notification.body: Body is building its calcium reserves. Enjoy that dairy! 🥛

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 30 – Brain Development Accelerates
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a large cabbage head – 39.9 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Brain develops its folds, increasing storage capacity. Eyes respond to light and dark. Lungs are nearly ready.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: The uterus has grown considerably. More frequent false contractions. General fatigue continues.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Start packing your hospital bag. Include medical documents, baby clothes, and your own essentials.
food_recommended: Iron to prevent anemia during delivery
pregnancy_weeks.medical: The Group B Streptococcus (GBS) test is done between weeks 35–37. Ask your doctor about it now.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Any fluid leaking from the vagina may be a broken water sac. Go to the ER immediately.

notification.title: 🧠 Brain in overdrive!
notification.body: 30 weeks! Baby is learning and remembering inside your womb! 🌙

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 31 – Nodding and Smiling
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby can now process information and track sounds. Swallows amniotic fluid to practice feeding.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Bladder pressure intensifies as baby pushes on it. Frequent nighttime bathroom trips disrupt sleep.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Avoid drinking large amounts of water right before bed, but don't reduce daytime intake.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Start counting daily fetal movements. 10 movements within 2 hours is a reassuring sign.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: No baby movement felt for over 2 hours after eating – call your doctor.

notification.title: 🥥 Weight is doubling!
notification.body: Baby gains 200g every week now. Growing so fast! ⚡

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 32 – Preparing for Birth
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a small cantaloupe – 42.4 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby begins positioning head-down for delivery. Lungs mature rapidly. Fat stores build up for the outside world.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Breathing difficulty increases as the uterus presses on the diaphragm. Belly may look slightly lower (lightening).
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Meditation and breathing sessions help you relax. Discuss your birth plan with your doctor now.
food_recommended: Dates (6 per day in the final weeks – proven to ease labor)
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Every-two-week prenatal visits. Discuss birth preferences, pain management, and delivery wishes.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: If baby is still breech (head up), discuss your options with your doctor.

notification.title: 🏁 8 weeks to go!
notification.body: Prepare your bag and your birth plan. It's getting close! 👜

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 33 – Lungs Nearly Complete
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Lungs are approaching full maturity. The immune system receives more antibodies from mom. Skin turns a healthy pink.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Heartburn is at its worst as the uterus presses hard on the stomach. Braxton Hicks are more frequent.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Eat very small meals and stay upright for at least two hours after eating. Chocolate and acidic drinks worsen heartburn.
food_recommended: Nuts and almonds as nutritious snacks
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Make sure your birth plan is formally documented in your medical file.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Regular painful contractions before week 37 = possible preterm labor. Go to the hospital immediately.

notification.title: 🍍 Lungs are complete!
notification.body: Every breath baby practices now will be their first breath of life 💨

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 34 – Final Organ Touches
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a small watermelon – 45 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Kidneys are fully functional. The central nervous system is complete. The fontanelle (soft spot in skull) stays flexible for birth.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Lightening reduces breathing pressure but increases pelvic pressure. Walking becomes harder.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Rest as much as possible. Place your left hand on your heart and right hand on your belly and talk to your baby.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Ask your doctor about signs of true labor: water breaking, bloody show, regular intensifying contractions.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Clear or pinkish fluid leaking from the vagina – head to the hospital immediately.

notification.title: 🔜 Meeting soon!
notification.body: 6 weeks or less! Your baby is almost ready to say hello 👋

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 35 – Nearly Complete
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a medium pumpkin – 46.2 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby is nearly fully developed. Fat deposits give the healthy, chubby newborn appearance. Twins typically arrive around this week.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Every step takes effort. Bathroom trips every 30 minutes. Insomnia is at its peak.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Prepare a list of emergency contacts (hospital, doctor, support person). Keep your phone charged at all times.
food_recommended: Daily dates to help ripen the cervix
Dietary iron to prevent post-birth bleeding
pregnancy_weeks.medical: GBS (Group B Strep) swab is done this week. A positive result means you'll need antibiotics during labor.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Sudden intense baby activity after a quiet period may signal fetal distress.

notification.title: ⏰ The clock is ticking!
notification.body: Your baby is almost ready. Is your bag ready too? 👜✅

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 36 – Final Preparations
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a large head of lettuce – 47.4 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Baby fills the uterus completely. Movements decrease but must still be felt. The placenta begins aging.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: You may feel intense pelvic heaviness. Full baby descent eases breathing pressure.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Do a home nesting sweep to prepare for your newborn. Set up your feeding station.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Weekly prenatal visits now. Doctor checks cervical dilation and effacement.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Less baby movement than usual – call your doctor right now.

notification.title: 🏠 Home ready? And baby?
notification.body: Final preparations! You're just steps away from meeting 🌸

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 37 – Full-Term Pregnancy
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a bunch of apricots – 48.6 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Pregnancy is officially full term! Baby clears meconium from intestines. Lungs are fully mature.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Labor can begin any time now! Signs: bloody show, regular contractions, water breaking.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Stay calm and alert. Time your contractions: if every 5 minutes for 1 hour, go to the hospital.
food_avoid: Heavy meals that make dealing with labor contractions harder
pregnancy_weeks.medical: If labor doesn't begin by week 42, your doctor will discuss labor induction options.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: If baby movements stop completely at any point = emergency hospital visit immediately.

notification.title: 🎊 Full term! Congratulations!
notification.body: Your baby is ready to meet you. Stay prepared! 🏥

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 38 – Any Moment Now
pregnancy_weeks.baby_size: Size of a small pumpkin – 49.8 cm
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Head hair is fully grown, fingernails are long. Meconium (first poop) is ready for after birth. The body releases birth hormones.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: You may feel a sudden surge of energy (nesting instinct) or the opposite – extreme fatigue.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: If you feel that energy surge, use it for rest, not cleaning! Your body needs every bit of energy for labor.
pregnancy_weeks.medical: Weekly visits. Doctor monitors baby via ultrasound to confirm placental function.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Any amniotic fluid leakage – go to the hospital immediately, even without contractions.

notification.title: 🤱 Any moment now!
notification.body: Get ready! Every hour could be the start of the birth journey 🌟

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 39 – The Moment Approaches
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Brain reaches final completion. Antibodies from mom protect baby in early months of life. Fully ready!
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: Cervix dilates and effaces. You may notice the mucus plug (bloody show) coming away.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Talk to your baby and tell them you're excited to meet them. Vocal soothing has a powerful effect even before birth.
food_avoid: Foods you know cause you bloating
pregnancy_weeks.medical: If you reach week 40 without labor, your doctor will closely monitor baby and discuss induction options.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: No baby movement or water breaking = go to the hospital immediately without delay.

notification.title: 💫 Tomorrow? The day after? Soon!
notification.body: A whole life is about to begin. You're ready, Mama 💕

pregnancy_weeks.title: Week 40 – The Long-Awaited Day
pregnancy_weeks.baby_development: Fully complete! Ready for the first cry of life. Lungs will open with the first breath. All body systems operate independently.
pregnancy_weeks.mother_changes: The journey is complete! Whether you deliver this week or slightly after, your body knows exactly what to do.
pregnancy_weeks.tips: Trust your body and your doctor. Vaginal or cesarean delivery – both take incredible courage. What matters is your safety and baby's health.
food_avoid: No strict restrictions now, but avoid heavy foods if you feel labor is near
pregnancy_weeks.medical: After 40+3 weeks, elective induction or close monitoring begins. Trust your doctor's decision.
pregnancy_weeks.warnings: Any decrease in fetal movement, any fluid, any bleeding = hospital immediately. Never hesitate.

notification.title: 👶 The big day is here!
notification.body: Congratulations! You'll meet the most beautiful thing in your life very soon 🌈💖
